explanation: Coniferous forests are located in the subarctic taiga, near high-altitude mountaintops, and along the Pacific Coast of North America. The taiga represents the classic coniferous forest, characterized by cone-bearing trees (conifers). These trees are highly adapted to freezing temperatures: their leaves and bark feature thick, protective coverings, and their needle-like leaves are structurally built to shed and withstand heavy snowfall. Additionally, the Pacific Northwest contains temperate rainforests (old-growth forests), which are evergreen coniferous forests. The organisms in these coniferous ecosystems are predominantly adapted to cold climates.

questions.q: What adaptations allow coniferous trees in the taiga to survive cold climates and heavy snow?
opts: Broad, thin leaves that drop off in winter
Leaves and bark with thick coverings, and needle-like leaves that withstand heavy snowfall
Fleshy, water-storing stems and shallow root networks
The ability to perform CAM photosynthesis at night
